kevin: quick dump from today's bench sweep — streaming (SSE) vs websocket for serving new q4_int8 models across regions (us-west1 / eu-west2 / ap-northeast1) on A100 / H100. short version: ws wins sustained throughput, sse slightly better p50 for single-shot tiny requests. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

bench-bot: scheduled job completed: run_id=2024-06-08-ksweep-09, configs tested: [mode: sse,ws] x [gpu: a100,h100] x [seq:128,512,1024] x [concurrency:16,64,256,1024] x [quant:fp16,q4_int8]

mira: some numbers from us-west1 (H100, seq=512):
- ws q4_int8 @ conc=256 => throughput ~ 78k tokens/sec, p50=14ms, p95=210ms
- sse q4_int8 @ conc=256 => throughput ~ 62k tokens/sec, p50=11ms, p95=340ms

ashok: interesting — p50 is lower for SSE because we short-circuit response chunks, but p95 jumps due to HTTP keepalive churn and proxy timeouts under bursty connect patterns. WS holds connections and batches better.

sara: metric from eu-west2 (A100, seq=1024, conc=64):
- ws fp16 => 31k toks/s, p50=23ms, p95=410ms
- ws q4_int8 => 42k toks/s, p50=19ms, p95=460ms (note: q4 helps throughput but introduced occasional kernel fallback on longer sequences which raised p95)

kevin: kernel note — on H100 we saw the runtime pick fused-flash kernels for fp16 at seq<=512. for q4_int8 it falls back to fallback-attn kernel in ~2% of steps when sequence crosses >768 tokens, causing a latency blip. file: /bench/logs/2024-06-08/ksweep-09/kernel-events.log

mira: reproducible command we used (small driver):
```
python perf_driver.py \
  --mode ws \
  --gpu h100 \
  --region us-west1 \
  --concurrency 256 \
  --seq 512 \
  --quant q4_int8 \
  --duration 300
```
use `--mode sse` to flip to SSE.

ashok: ops notes — for streaming endpoints we observed a ~12% reduction in per-token cost due to KV/prefix cache hits when requests share prefixes. that benefit is bigger for SSE because we stream partial tokens and more requests ended up reusing cached prefixes in our synthetic workload.

sara: region diff: ap-northeast1 had slightly worse p95 (H100 q4_int8 conc=512 p95 ~ 520ms) likely due to noisy neighbors on the test cluster; repeatable if you pin instance soft-affinity.

kevin: recommendations summary:
- Use WebSocket for high sustained concurrency / throughput workloads (>=128 concurrent streams). better batching and connection reuse.
- Use SSE for low-latency single-shot flows (p50 advantage) and where proxied HTTP stacks are stable.
- For q4_int8: big throughput wins (1.3-1.5x) on A100/H100, but validate kernel fallbacks on >768 seq. add a regression guard in model onboarding evals that flags q4 when fallback_rate > 0.5%.
- Tune keepalive and proxy timeouts for SSE to avoid tail spikes under bursty connects.

mira: I'll upload the full CSV and the charts to the bench drive (folder: /bench/2024-06/ksweep-09) and add a filterable notebook with the per-region heatmaps.

ashok: one more gotcha — when you enable server side batching for WS we saw p95 go up slightly at low conc because of batching delay; set a dynamic batch-window that is smaller when observed concurrency < 64.

kevin: thanks all. next step: run a follow-up with seq=2048 on H100 pinned infra to verify q4 fallback behavior, and a short APAC re-run with isolated nodes. assigning @mira to queue the runs and @ashok to add the q4 fallback check into the onboarding CI. :white_check_mark:
